headline: Secure Desert Glamping and Chisos Basin Permits Early
reservation: Entry to the ghost town is open, but nearby Big Bend National Park requires separate entry fees. Accommodation in Terlingua, especially glamping and restored cabins, often fills six to nine months in advance for spring. Changing permit systems for park backcountry and river access require checking the official National Park Service site.

days.title: Mercury Mines and Ghost Town Ruins
days.start: Suggested: 9 AM from Terlingua Ghost Town

stops.name: Terlingua Cemetery
stops.detail: Walk among the historic hand-placed stone markers that document the town's mining history.

stops.name: Starlight Theatre
stops.detail: Visit this iconic local landmark, originally a roofless theater for miners, now a social hub.

days.driving: Minimal local driving; allow for unpaved terrain between sites.
days.note: Expect high dust levels and limited shade while walking the ruins.

days.title: Chihuahuan Desert Vistas

stops.name: Santa Elena Canyon Overlook
stops.detail: View the dramatic 1,500-foot limestone walls where the Rio Grande cuts through the Mesa de Anguila.

stops.name: Ross Maxwell Scenic Drive
stops.detail: Observe the volcanic history of the region via geologic pull-outs leading toward the river.

days.driving: Allow 2–3 hours round trip; conditions vary by weather.
days.note: High clearance vehicles are recommended for any desert spur roads.

days.title: High Basin and Low River

stops.name: Chisos Basin
stops.detail: Transition from desert flats to mountain woodlands for views of the Window pouroff.

stops.name: Lajitas River Access
stops.detail: Visit the nearby gateway to the Rio Grande for river views near the state park border.

days.driving: Allow 3 hours total travel; mountain roads are steep and winding.
days.note: Parking in the Basin frequently fills; arrive early or use local shuttles if available.

intel.title: Ghost Town Congestion
intel.text: Parking near the Ghost Town area is informal and fills during the annual chili cook-offs. Use designated pull-offs and avoid blocking narrow dirt access roads.

intel.title: Remote Connectivity
intel.text: Cellular service is extremely spotty throughout West Texas and absent in many canyon areas. Download offline maps and official park apps before leaving Alpine or Marfa.

intel.title: Study Butte Supplies
intel.text: Fuel is available in Study Butte and Lajitas, but distance between stations is significant. Always refuel before entering the national park for the day.

intel.title: Seasonal Heat Windows
intel.text: Midday temperatures regularly exceed 100 degrees from May through September. Limit strenuous outdoor activities to the hours before 10 AM to avoid heat exhaustion.

intel.title: Unpaved Road Hazards
intel.text: Many glamping sites and local sights are accessed via washboard gravel roads. Check rental agreements for restrictions on unpaved surfaces before driving to remote camps.

plan.arrival: Pick up your rental at Midland (MAF), stop for bulk groceries and water in Alpine, then complete the final two-hour drive to Terlingua.
plan.vehicle: A sturdy SUV is preferred for desert wind and washboard roads; check rental restrictions for off-pavement travel.
plan.goldenHour: The Window View in the Chisos Basin is a classic sunset spot, though colors vary seasonally with atmospheric dust.
